intro: Searching for planning consultants near you usually means something has prompted a decision about a property — an extension you are unsure about, a refusal you want to understand, or a site you hope to develop. You want someone local who knows the council's policies and can tell you honestly what is realistic. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK planning consultant who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for planning consultants near them usually need
need_lead: Most enquiries come from people facing a specific planning question and wanting local knowledge before they commit.
needs: You are thinking about an extension, loft conversion or change of use and want to know whether it stands a chance under your council's local plan policies.
You have had an application refused and need help understanding the reasons and whether an appeal is worth pursuing.
You want pre-application advice prepared and taken to the council to reduce the risk of a refusal later.
You are buying a property or site and need a view on whether your intended plans are realistic before you exchange.
You have a scheme that needs coordinating with architects, surveyors or specialists such as heritage, ecology or highways experts and want someone to steer it.
context: Planning decisions turn on your council's local plan policies and the specifics of your site, so a consultant who regularly works in your area will know the local policy landscape and how the planning authority tends to approach similar proposals. Pre-application advice is often worth the effort because it reduces risk before you submit.

Many planning consultants are chartered members of the Royal Town Planning Institute, shown by the letters MRTPI, and follow the RTPI's code of professional conduct. You can check the RTPI directory before appointing anyone, and a good consultant will tell you early whether a scheme is realistic under local policy rather than promising an outcome.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe the property or site and what you want to do, including whether it is a house, a flat, a commercial premises or land.
Give the location or postcode area so we can introduce a consultant who works in that area.
Say where you are in the process — just exploring, preparing an application, responding to a refusal, or considering an appeal.
Mention any deadlines you are aware of, particularly around appeals, so timing can be discussed.
Explain whether architects, surveyors or other specialists are already involved and what stage their work has reached.
Set out what you most want from the consultant, such as pre-application advice, a full application, appeal support or a feasibility view.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the planning consultant
questions: How familiar are you with my local planning authority's local plan policies and this type of proposal?
What would you recommend as the first step — pre-application advice, a feasibility assessment or preparing an application?
What have you handled that is similar to my situation, and what did it involve?
How will you keep me informed about progress and the council's responses?
What would you need from me, and from my architect or other specialists, to get started?
If the application is refused, what are the appeal deadlines and how would you approach an appeal?

faqs.q: Do I need a planning consultant or just an architect?
faqs.a: Architects design the scheme, while planning consultants focus on planning policy, applications, appeals and negotiation with the council. For anything beyond straightforward permitted development, a consultant's knowledge of local policy can be valuable, and the two often work together.

faqs.q: What is pre-application advice and is it worth it?
faqs.a: It is advice sought from the council before you submit a formal application, intended to reduce risk and reveal issues early. Whether it is worthwhile depends on the complexity of your proposal, and a consultant can advise on that for your site.

faqs.q: How do I judge which planning consultant to choose near me?
faqs.a: Ask about their experience with your local authority and similar proposals, check whether they are an MRTPI chartered member through the RTPI directory, and compare the quotes you receive. Fees are on application, so ask each consultant to set out what is included.

faqs.q: What happens if my application is refused?
faqs.a: There are routes to challenge a refusal, including appeal, and appeals have deadlines that must be met. A planning consultant can go through the decision notice with you and advise on the options and timing.
